pairs.locus: Lhomond, De Viris Illustribus, Lucius Tarquinius Priscus (Accius Navius)
pairs.question: Atqui hoc agitabam an cotem illam secare novacula possem.
pairs.derivation: The king tests the augur's claim that what he is silently thinking can be done. Stripped the speech tags 'inquit rex' and 'inquit augur'; the narrative 'et secuisse dicitur' follows and is omitted. The king's words contain the indirect interrogative 'an ... possem' (whether he could cut the whetstone); 'Potes ergo' genuinely answers it (you can).

pairs.locus: Lhomond, De Viris Illustribus, Publius Valerius Laevinus (Cineas and Pyrrhus)
pairs.question: Superatis Romanis, quid agere destinas, O rex?
pairs.answer: Italiae vicina est Sicilia, nec difficile erit eam armis occupare.
pairs.derivation: First exchange of the Cineas/Pyrrhus dialogue chain. Took only the first Q&A pair (clean and self-contained); dropped the speech tags 'respondit Cineas' (already absent here) and 'inquit Pyrrhus' from the answer. The later questions ('Occupata Sicilia, quid postea acturus es?', 'Quid deinde?', 'Quin tu isto otio jam nunc frueris?') are separate exchanges, not joined.

pairs.locus: Lhomond, De Viris Illustribus, Aulus Atilius Calatinus (Calpurnius)
pairs.question: Fidum quidem et providum hoc consilium videtur; sed quisnam erit qui ducat quadringentos illos milites ad eum locum?
pairs.answer: Si alium neminem reperis, me ad hoc consilium perficiendum uti potes. Ego hanc tibi et reipublicae animam do.
pairs.derivation: Quoted the consul's full reply as the question (whole-utterance preserved): it accepts the plan then asks who will lead the 400 men. Calpurnius answers that he himself will. Stripped 'Respondit consul:' and the inline 'inquit Calpurnius'. Kept both answer sentences as a contiguous span.

pairs.locus: Lhomond, De Viris Illustribus, Publius Cornelius Scipio Africanus (Scipio and Hannibal)
pairs.question: Quidnam igitur tu diceres, si me vicisses?
pairs.answer: Me vero et ante Alexandrum et ante Pyrrhum et ante alios omnes posuissem.
pairs.derivation: Final, direct-speech turn of the Scipio/Hannibal ranking-of-generals exchange (the earlier turns are reported indirectly, so dropped). Stripped the tags 'Tum ridens Scipio:' / 'inquit' and 'respondit Annibal'. Hannibal's reply genuinely answers the hypothetical.

pairs.locus: Lhomond, De Viris Illustribus, Publius Scipio Nasica (Nasica the censor)
pairs.question: Quidnam causae est cur sis tu, quam equus pinguior?
pairs.answer: Quoniam ego me ipse curo, equum vero servus.
pairs.derivation: Census-review exchange. Stripped 'inquit censor' and 'respondit eques'. The eques genuinely answers why he is fatter than his horse (he tends himself, a slave tends the horse). Following narration 'Minus verecundum visum est responsum...' omitted.

pairs.locus: Lhomond, De Viris Illustribus, Lucius Paulus Aemilius Macedonicus (Paulus and Tertia)
pairs.question: Quid est, mea Tertia, quid tristis es?
pairs.derivation: Father asks his little daughter why she is sad; she answers that Perse (her puppy) has died. Stripped the tags 'inquit' and 'inquit illa'. The parenthetical gloss '(Erat autem mortua catella eo nomine)' and the reply 'Accipio omen' are narration/next-turn and omitted; the answer genuinely answers the question.

pairs.locus: Lhomond, De Viris Illustribus, Tiberius Gracchus et Caius Gracchus (Gracchus and Piso)
pairs.question: Qui tibi constas, Piso, cum ea lege frumentum petas quam dissuasisti?
pairs.answer: Nolim quidem, Grache, mea bona tibi viritim dividere liceat: sed si facias, partem petam.
pairs.derivation: Gracchus challenges Piso for taking grain under a law Piso opposed; Piso answers. Stripped 'eum sic compellavit...' (framing) and 'Cui Piso:' / 'inquit'. The question is self-contained ('ea lege ... quam dissuasisti' identifies the grain law).

pairs.locus: Lhomond, De Viris Illustribus, Tiberius Gracchus et Caius Gracchus (the consul and Blosius)
pairs.question: Quid? si te in Capitolium faces ferre vellet, obsecuturusne voluntati illius fuisses propter istam quam jactas familiaritatem?
pairs.answer: Nunquam id quidem voluisset; sed, si voluisset, paruissem.
pairs.derivation: The consul asks Blosius whether he would have obeyed Gracchus even to burn the Capitol; Blosius answers. Stripped 'Tum consul:' / 'ait' and 'inquit Blosius'. The interrogative 'obsecuturusne ... fuisses' is genuinely answered ('paruissem').

pairs.locus: Lhomond, De Viris Illustribus, Cnaeus Pompeius Magnus (Catulus and the assembly)
pairs.question: Si quid ei acciderit, ecquemnam in ejus locum substituetis?
pairs.derivation: Catulus, opposing the grant of extraordinary command to Pompey, asks the assembly whom they would put in his place; the whole assembly answers. 'ei'/'ejus' = Pompeius (subject of the surrounding narration). Stripped 'Acclamavit universa contio:'. Genuine interrogative ('ecquemnam') and direct answer.

pairs.locus: Lhomond, De Viris Illustribus, Caius Julius Caesar (Caesar and the helmsman)
pairs.question: Quid times?
pairs.derivation: Caesar, crossing in a storm, rebukes the frightened helmsman with a question he immediately answers himself. Both clauses are Caesar's own words quoted directly; stripped the tag 'ait'. A genuine interrogative with its genuine answer in the same utterance.
